thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: SRV-502 smart-routing fallback loop detected in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Customers: high-throughput tenants reporting 5xxs and increased latency.
Neha (on-call): I'm on it. paging Neha -> acknowledged. grabbing logs and dashboard.
Neha (on-call): saw a spike in fallback-to-variant B after region failover started at ~2023-12-07T14:02:00Z. headers show X-Route-Policy:force-region.
Sam (sre): looking — routing policy engine is returning match to 'variant-b-quant' even though policy should prefer 'variant-a'. possibly config drift after the last rollout.
Jorge (infra): I see a manual force-region override executed by deploy-bot earlier: `force-region us-west-2 --until 2023-12-07T15:00Z` from console. who triggered that?
Maria (product): that was me, I forced region to stabilize a customer in eu-west but I accidentally targeted us-west in the UI. I thought I clicked eu-west. :grimace:
Neha (on-call): ok, that explains why a subset of traffic was pinned. The problem is forcing region caused the smart-routing to map to a model variant incompatible with current capacity -> fallback kicks in -> circuit creates loop between variants and regions.
Sam (sre): logs: repeated entries: `Eligible variants: [variant-a, variant-b-quant], selected: variant-b-quant, kv-cache-miss -> fallback to variant-a -> selected: variant-b-quant` — looks like sticky-policy negotiation bug.
Neha (on-call): Customer impact: elevated 5xxs for streaming endpoints and spikes in token latency for 3 tenants. Engaging mitigation options: 1) revert force-region, 2) pin model back to variant-a globally, 3) enable emergency fallback-off policy.
Jorge (infra): we can revert the force-region from the audit action. deploy-bot can roll back. but it might be safer to remove the force-region first and let routing reclaim normal state.
Neha (on-call): +1. I'm going to undo the region force now. Doing: `/deploy-bot rollback-action 2023456001` (this is the action id).
deploy-bot: Action rollback initiated by Neha. Rolling back force-region us-west-2 -> eu-west-1. ETA ~15s.
incident-bot: NOTE: rolling back regional pin may cause transient request reroutes. Prepare to monitor for additional 5xxs.
Sam (sre): After rollback, we still see repeated variant flips. hypothesis: a different policy (force-model pin) was applied as a hotpatch earlier, making sticky variant selection incompatible. check policy history.
Neha (on-call): searching policy history... found `force-model variant-b-quant` applied at 2023456700 by sprint-squad during a quick canary patch. It didn't appear in the main audit because it was an emergency CLI hotpatch.
Maria (product): that hotpatch was to address higher memory usage but it was supposed to be scoped to low-traffic buckets. Oops.
Jorge (infra): manual force-model + force-region created a combinatorial effect: routing engine applies force-model then reroutes to forced region which lacks capacity for that quantized variant -> fallback to other variant -> some requests loop back.
Neha (on-call): current mitigation: disable emergency hotpatch `force-model` and remove fallback sticky behaviour temporarily. I'll execute emergency-unset on the model pin.
Neha (on-call): running: `/policy unset force-model variant-b-quant --actor Neha --reason "incident mitigation"`
Sam (sre): warning: unsetting the model pin will change live traffic mix. We should coordinate with DC ops in case any hardware hot-cache needs warming.
Neha (on-call): acknowledged. doing it now.
Neha (on-call): done. policy unset confirmed by deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Policy change applied: force-model variant-b-quant removed by Neha. Change id 2023456810.
Sam (sre): immediate telemetry: 500s dropping ~70% within 2 minutes. latency returning to baseline for most tenants; small residual for one customer.
Maria (product): contacting the affected customer (acct: NMR-42) — giving ETA 30 min and describing rollback actions.
Neha (on-call): I'm going to keep an eye on sticky token caches and routing logs for 15 minutes. If stable, we'll revert any temporary policy toggles and run a postmortem.
Sam (sre): next steps: 1) incident containment complete, 2) record timeline and actor IDs, 3) schedule postmortem with product and infra, 4) run a small audit of CLI hotpatches to avoid non-audited emergency changes.
Jorge (infra): I'll work on a patch to have the routing engine surface combined policy conflicts as warnings (force-region + force-model) so future hotpatches warn people.
Maria (product): agree. also we need UI guardrails to confirm region selection. I'll file a JIRA.
Neha (on-call): handing off to Sam for the rest of suppression and post-incident follow-ups. Sam, you own the postmortem. I'm marking incident as mitigated in the channel but will stay available for handoff.
Sam (sre): taking over. Thanks Neha. I will run a 1-hour watch and then move to postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: SRV-502 mitigated (manual overrides reverted). Incident closed for active paging at 2023-12-07T14:12:00Z.
Neha (on-call): note for postmortem: manual override paths need clearer audit and rollback tooling; consider a "preview" step that shows combined policy interactions.
Maria (product): thanks everyone. I'll attach customer comms draft to the incident doc.
Sam (sre): filing postmortem ticket now.
